profile.reading: This is Polcoms Skawina data center, near Krakow in southern Poland, put into service in 2011. Polcom, a Polish IT infrastructure and cloud computing company, describes the facility as spanning about 6,000 square meters with 15 megawatts of power capacity and the ability to deliver up to 15 kilowatts per rack for high density colocation customers. The site holds ISO 27001:2017 information security, ISO 27017:2015 cloud security, and ISO 9001:2015 quality management certifications. Skawina forms one half of Polcoms two site Krakow area data center network, paired with a second facility at Alwernia between Krakow and Katowice, allowing the company to offer redundant colocation, cloud computing, and IT integration services with georedundancy across both sites for enterprise and public sector clients in southern Poland. Polcom describes itself as having more than 30 years in the market, with its first data center completed in 2006 before Skawina and Alwernia followed as its second and later locations, headquartered at ul. Krakowska 43 in Skawina itself. The company reports over 300 business customers, about 70 percent with international reach across four continents, spanning finance, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, e-commerce, and public sector clients, supported by a staff of about 170 specialists, and holds Polands Polska Chmura, or Polish Cloud, certification alongside compliance with the European Cloud Sovereignty Framework. Combined, the Skawina and Alwernia sites total more than 12,000 square meters across roughly 6 hectares of secured, fenced plots, linked by independent fiber optic cable over the 24 kilometers separating them, and the Alwernia facility cost about 63 million Polish zloty to build, using direct liquid cooling technology that Polcom engineers paired with a proprietary heat recovery system for pipeline fluids, achieving a power usage effectiveness below 1.2 and cutting water heating energy consumption by about 10 percent.
